postTitle: Is 0% EMI or Buy Now Pay Later Really Free? When Free Is Free
topic: 0% interest can still cost you: a balance left at a deadline, a late or failed payment, fees on top

assumptions.notes: Lesson: deferred interest (some plans charge interest back to the purchase date if any balance is left at the deadline; €1,200, €120 left, about €176 at 25%, left out: council Nov 5, the figure needs its schedule and rate). Bars are not to scale of any plan. Late or failed payments bring fees, and on some plans switch the plan to interest; processing fees and tax on hidden interest. Numbers: 0%, €1,200.

hookVariants.narration: Part two: zero percent interest can still cost you.

beats.narration: Twelve hundred euros, at zero percent until a deadline.
A small balance is left at the deadline.
On some plans, interest is then charged from purchase day, on the whole purchase, not just what is left. That is called deferred interest.
Also check late or failed payments, and fees or taxes on top.

caption.instagram:
0% interest can still cost you. Three lines in the fine print.

€1,200 bought at 0% until a deadline. The monthly payments leave a small balance at the deadline. On some plans, interest is then charged from purchase day, on the whole purchase, not just what is left. That is called deferred interest.

A late or failed payment can bring a fee, or on some plans, interest. And there can be fees on the plan: processing fees, and any taxes that apply.
